pairs.question: Quorsus igitur haec tam multa de Maximo?
pairs.answer: Quia profecto videtis nefas esse dictu miseram fuisse talem senectutem.
pairs.derivation: Cato poses his own question and answers it. The answer is the single sentence following the question; it ends at the full stop before 'Nec tamen omnes possunt esse Scipiones...', which turns to elaboration. Verbatim and contiguous.

pairs.question: cum ex eo quaereretur, cur tam diu vellet esse in vita
pairs.derivation: Gorgias's reported question why he wished to live so long (verbatim indirect-question clause kept with its 'cum ... quaereretur' setup) answered by his quoted reply. Speech tag 'inquit' dropped from mid-quote; the reply is contiguous to its full stop, before 'Praeclarum responsum...'.

pairs.question: quaerenti, cui serat
pairs.answer: Dis immortalibus, qui me non accipere modo haec a maioribus voluerunt, sed etiam posteris prodere.
pairs.derivation: The farmer is asked for whom he plants (verbatim indirect-question clause 'cui serat' kept with its 'quaerenti' setup) and answers in quoted speech. Speech-verb 'respondere' dropped; the quoted answer is taken whole.

pairs.question: cum ex eo quaereret, utereturne rebus veneriis
pairs.answer: Di meliora! libenter vero istinc sicut ab domino agresti ac furioso profugi.
pairs.derivation: Reported question to Sophocles (the verbatim interrogative clause 'utereturne rebus veneriis' kept with its 'cum ... quaereret' setup for intelligibility) answered by his quoted reply. Speech tag 'inquit' dropped; answer ends at the full stop before 'Cupidis enim...', which generalizes.

pairs.question: Quorsus hoc?
pairs.answer: Ut intellegeretis, si voluptatem aspernari ratione et sapientia non possemus, magnam habendam esse senectuti gratiam, quae efficeret, ut id non liberet, quod non operteret.
pairs.derivation: Cato's own purpose-question answered with a purpose clause. Answer ends at the full stop before 'Impedit enim consilium voluptas...', which elaborates. Verbatim and contiguous.

pairs.question: Quorsus igitur tam multa de voluptate?
pairs.answer: Quia non modo vituperatio nulla, sed etiam summa laus senectutis est, quod ea voluptates nullas magno opere desiderat.
pairs.derivation: Cato poses and answers his own question. Answer ends at the full stop before 'Caret epulis...', which elaborates. Verbatim and contiguous.

pairs.question: tum eum dixisse mirari se non modo diligentiam, sed etiam sollertiam eius, a quo essent illa dimensa atque discripta
pairs.answer: Atqui ego ista sum omnia dimensus; mei sunt ordines, mea discriptio, multae etiam istarum arborum mea manu sunt satae.
pairs.derivation: Lysander's reported question who laid out the garden (verbatim indirect-question clause kept for intelligibility) answered by Cyrus's quoted reply. Speech tag 'et Cyrum respondisse' dropped; the quoted answer is taken whole to its full stop.

pairs.question: cum illi quaerenti, qua tandem re fretus sibi tam audaciter obsisteret
pairs.derivation: Pisistratus's reported question to Solon (verbatim interrogative clause kept with its 'cum ... quaerenti' setup) answered by Solon's one-word quoted reply. Speech tag 'respondisse dicitur' dropped.
